experiment: Renovate OpenTelemetry to bounded Prometheus metrics

configuration.selection: Same deterministic nested cohort for control and instrumented scans
configuration.credential: Read-only GitHub App installation token scoped to the exact 25 repositories
configuration.transport: Renovate OTLP/HTTP traces to OpenTelemetry Collector; spanmetrics connector to Prometheus OTLP receiver

excluded_initial_run.reason: Both Renovate scans and the telemetry pipeline succeeded, but the parser incorrectly required calls_total for the run span. Duration count and duration sum proved the run span existed.
excluded_initial_run.observed_problem: Unfiltered spanmetrics used high-cardinality span names containing repository paths, branch names and raw commands.

interpretation.cardinality_reduction: 1305 to 105 series for the same 25-repository cohort
interpretation.overhead: The valid instrumented scan was eight seconds slower than its control. One paired run is insufficient for a stable percentage estimate, but no material execution boundary was approached.
interpretation.prometheus_alone_is_insufficient: Renovate emitted traces; OpenTelemetry Collector spanmetrics converted them into Prometheus metrics.

limitations: The performance comparison is one paired run with update-heavy dry-run work and normal runner variance.
Renovate OpenTelemetry support and the Collector spanmetrics connector can evolve; immutable version pinning and upgrade validation remain necessary.
The experiment used an ephemeral Prometheus instance and did not validate long-term storage, dashboards, alert delivery or a managed observability vendor.
Detailed high-cardinality traces were intentionally filtered before spanmetrics in this lab. A production trace backend may retain full traces while generating only bounded metrics.
